_what: The credit-bundle shelf as DRAWN on the Credits boards, plus the rule that decides which row may carry BEST VALUE. Frozen here because CI cannot reach Penpot — exactly like penpot-pairs.json. `npm run check:credits` asserts this file against the economy rule, so a price change cannot land without the badge moving with it.
_refresh: Re-run penpot-sweeps/credits-best-value.js after any price change: it reads the boards, recomputes, and prints this file.

lockedRate.source: doc 10 line 13 · doc 09 §7.7 — US$1.55 per 1,000 credits (break-even $1.19 + 30% worst-case margin). PM-locked 2026-09-26.

floor.rule: doc 10: 'bundles must average ≥ floor' — a volume discount may never take a bundle below $1.19/1,000.

_photoFee: doc 10: one photo offering costs 150 credits — the second locked number the page is built on, used for the ≈ N offerings lines.
bestValueRule: argmin(priceCents / credits) — the cheapest credit per 1,000. Tie-break: SMALLEST credits, i.e. the cheapest way to reach the best rate, and the least commitment to ask of a user. Switch the tie-break to 'largest' to prefer the biggest absolute bundle; the formula itself does not change.
_asDrawn: On 2026-10-10 the ladder is LINEAR at the locked rate, so 1,000 / 3,000 / 6,000 / 10,000 all tie at exactly $1.55 per 1,000 and the 500 is the only bundle worse than the rate ($1.56, because 155¢ × 500 = 77.5¢ rounds UP to 78¢). ⚠️ So BEST VALUE on the 1,000 row is the TIE-BREAK's answer, not a unique fact — a volume discount (permitted down to $1.19) is what would make it unique, and that is a pricing decision, not a labelling one.
